units.text: INT. SUPERMAN - CONTINUOUS
Now, Ann, I do beg you not to put it on me. I have no opinion on the subject; and if I had, it would probably not be attended to. I am quite with whatever you three think best.
units.name: MRS WHITEFIELD

units.text: Tanner turns his head and looks fixedly at Ramsden, who angrily refuses to receive this mute communication.
resuming in the same gentle voice, ignoring her mother's bad taste.

Mamma knows that she is not strong enough to bear the whole responsibility for me and Rhoda without some help and advice. Rhoda must have a guardian; and though I am older, I do not think any young unmarried woman should be left quite to her own guidance. I hope you agree with me, Granny?
units.name: ANN

units.text: starting.
Granny! Do you intend to call your guardians Granny?
units.name: TANNER

units.text: Don't be foolish, Jack. Mr Ramsden has always been Grandpapa Roebuck to me: I am Granny's Annie; and he is Annie's Granny. I christened him so when I first learned to speak.
units.name: ANN

units.text: sarcastically.
I hope you are satisfied, Mr Tanner. Go on, Annie: I quite agree with you.
units.name: RAMSDEN

units.text: Well, if I am to have a guardian, CAN I set aside anybody whom my dear father appointed for me?
units.name: ANN

units.text: biting his lip.
You approve of your father's choice, then?
units.name: RAMSDEN

units.text: It is not for me to approve or disapprove. I accept it. My father loved me and knew best what was good for me.
units.name: ANN

units.text: Of course I understand your feeling, Annie. It is what I should have expected of you; and it does you credit. But it does not settle the question so completely as you think. Let me put a case to you. Suppose you were to discover that I had been guilty of some disgraceful action--that I was not the man your poor dear father took me for. Would you still consider it right that I should be Rhoda's guardian?
units.name: RAMSDEN

units.text: I can't imagine you doing anything disgraceful, Granny.
units.name: ANN

units.text: to Ramsden.
You haven't done anything of the sort, have you?
units.name: TANNER

units.text: indignantly.
No sir.
units.name: RAMSDEN

units.text: placidly.
Well, then, why suppose it?
units.name: MRS. WHITEFIELD

units.text: You see, Granny, Mamma would not like me to suppose it.
units.name: ANN

units.text: much perplexed.
You are both so full of natural and affectionate feeling in these family matters that it is very hard to put the situation fairly before you.
units.name: RAMSDEN

units.text: Besides, my friend, you are not putting the situation fairly before them.
units.name: TANNER

units.text: sulkily.
Put it yourself, then.
units.name: RAMSDEN

units.text: I will. Ann: Ramsden thinks I am not fit be your guardian; and I quite agree with him. He considers that if your father had read my book, he wouldn't have appointed me. That book is the disgraceful action he has been talking about. He thinks it's your duty for Rhoda's sake to ask him to act alone and to make me withdraw. Say the word and I will.
units.name: TANNER

units.text: But I haven't read your book, Jack.
units.name: ANN

units.text: diving at the waste-paper basket and fishing the book out for her.
Then read it at once and decide.
units.name: TANNER

units.text: If I am to be your guardian, I positively forbid you to read that book, Annie.
units.name: RAMSDEN

units.text: He smites the table with his fist and rises.
Of course, if you don't wish it.
units.name: ANN

units.text: She puts the book on the table.
If one guardian is to forbid you to read the other guardian's book, how are we to settle it? Suppose I order you to read it! What about your duty to me?
units.name: TANNER

units.text: gently.
I am sure you would never purposely force me into a painful dilemma, Jack.
units.name: ANN

units.text: irritably.
Yes, yes, Annie: this is all very well, and, as I said, quite natural and becoming. But you must make a choice one way or the other. We are as much in a dilemma as you.
units.name: RAMSDEN

units.text: I feel that I am too young, too inexperienced, to decide. My father's wishes are sacred to me.
units.name: ANN

units.text: If you two men won't carry them out I must say it is rather hard that you should put the responsibility on Ann. It seems to me that people are always putting things on other people in this world.
units.name: MRS WHITEFIELD

units.text: I am sorry you take it that way.
units.name: RAMSDEN

units.text: touchingly.
Do you refuse to accept me as your ward, Granny?
units.name: ANN
